prompt:
Pixel art for a 16-bit style side-view arena shooter that runs at 640x360. Edit the attached template in place: it is drawn on a chunky pixel grid where one art pixel is exactly 1/240 of the image width; keep exactly that pixel size (never finer, never subdivided), and keep every size anchor and guide position. Crisp hard pixels: a clean 1-pixel near-black outline around every character, Enemy and prop; flat cel shading with 3-4 tones per material, shadows leaning purple-blue and highlights leaning warm yellow, light from the upper left; no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no blur, no soft edges, no semi-transparent pixels (use a checkerboard dither for any in-between tone). Characters are seen in a three-quarter side view (Metal Slug style): facing right, head and chest turned slightly toward the viewer. No text, no watermark, no shadows on the ground unless asked.

Image 1 is the template to edit. On the far left stands Rexi, a 64-pixel-tall judge: he is only the size anchor, leave him exactly as he is. The three light grey boxes (one at the top right, two along the bottom) each hold a small rough draft of the same Enemy, the "Banca Artillada", a heavy boss gunship. Redraw the draft in every box as finished, detailed pixel art that fills its box: about 102 pixels wide and 48 pixels tall, never past the box edges, the three copies identical in design and not touching. Image 2 is the concept art for this Enemy: follow its design, shapes and materials, but never its size. Keep exactly the template's pixel size.

The Banca Artillada, facing right, seen from the side and almost symmetric: a red weight bench press turned into a twin-rotor gunship.
1) A long padded red bench with stitched seams and glossy highlights, on a black steel frame.
2) In the bench's front (right) end, a glass canopy, light blue with a white glint, holding a tiny gym-bro pilot: brown hair, a red headband, a black tank top, a big grin.
3) Above the bench, a chrome barbell rests across the rack, loaded at both ends with black iron weight plates that stick out past the bench ends.
4) The rack's two black uprights continue up as rotor masts, each topped by a red rotor motor with a small dark hub. NO rotor blades and no rotor disc: the rotors are animated in code.
5) A red rocket pod with four dark launch tubes hangs under each end of the bench, and a dark engine housing with a grille sits under the middle of the bench.
Red in four tones from a deep maroon shadow to a coral highlight; black steel with blue-grey highlights. Plain white background, no flames, no smoke, no shadow under it.
